title: Brookside Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Brookside Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered architecture, security requirements (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), private deployment options (VPC vs Dedicated), initial pilot scope and success metrics. Agreed next steps: share security pack, schedule technical deep dive for networking and benchmarks, provide test account and onboarding timeline.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + security pack (Priya) by 2027-02-28
Schedule deep technical session with Brookside infra team (Ethan) - target week of 3/8
Provision test API keys + sandbox tenant (Jared) by 2027-03-02
Customer to share list of PII/data residency needs (Maya) by 2027-03-01
action_items: Priya Kapoor: Send SOC2 and security documentation : 2027-02-28
Ethan Liu: Schedule and run technical deep dive on VPC peering and benchmarking : 2027-03-10

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Brookside VP Eng), Carlos (Brookside DevOps), Anita (PM), Samir (Security)

Summary: Quick intros, alignment on infra and security needs, discussion of deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), pilot scope and success criteria. 

[00:00] Jared: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jared from Redwood, i run the AE for this account, with priya and ethan from our CS and SE teams. how are you all?
[00:06] Maya: good thanks, yeah excited to kick this off, we've been looking forward to this.
[00:10] Carlos: hey all.
[00:12] Anita: hi, thanks.
[00:15] Priya: quick round robin — we'll do roles, then high level plan. 
[00:22] Ethan: hi i'm ethan, i handle infra integ, we'll go deep into networking and benchmarks when we get to that section. 
[00:30] Samir: samir - security, i'll grill you on encryption, audit logs, things like that. 

[02:02] Jared: great, so high level goal, brookside wants to add genai features to the patient portal for triage and internal docs summarization, initial scope is triage bot and clinician note summarization, target pilot in 6 weeks, does that still hold?
[02:20] Maya: yup 6 weeks is the target but we have two constraints — first SOC2 compliance and SSO with our Okta instance, second is data residency, about half our data needs to stay in us-east-1.
[02:35] Jared: understood. priya i'll hand to you to talk onboarding flow, then ethan to follow on privately deployment options.

[05:00] Priya: onboarding flow — week 0 we do kickoff (today), week 1 tech deep dive + env setup, week 2 sandbox testing, week 3 pilot scale and benchmarks, week 4 wrap and go/no-go. we'll be flexible but that's the default.
[05:20] Anita: sounds good, are we doing hosted or dedicated?
[05:28] Ethan: good question — short answer: for pilot we recommend hosted with private routing to us-east region to move fast, but because of your data residency and SOC2, you'll likely move to Dedicated or Private (VPC) for production. tradeoffs: hosted is fastest and lowest ops, dedicated gives predictable throughput, private/VPC meets strict network controls.

[07:40] Carlos: for us the main gap is VPC peering and audit logging. we need the traffic to not transit public internet, and we need kinesis-style audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. can redwood support VPC peering and syslog?
[08:05] Ethan: yes we support VPC peering for Private deployment and for Dedicated we can do private endpoints. audit logs — we can stream logs to your S3 or push to a syslog endpoint, we have hooks for that. small caveat: hosted public API does not do VPC peering, but we do row-level guarantees and encryption at rest.

[10:20] Samir: encryption — we need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and all logs to be encrypted. do you support CMEK?
[10:30] Priya: yes CMKs supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted can use KMS with per-tenant keys but not customer HSM in the first rollout.
[10:45] Samir: ok and do you have SOC2 type 2?
[10:48] Jared: yes we have SOC 2 Type II, iso 27001 in progress, we'll send the security pack.

[13:00] Maya: we also have strict PII constraints — certain PHI elements must not be stored longer than X days and must not leave the region. can we set TTL or disable persistent logging of model inputs?
[13:20] Ethan: we can set retention policies and we have config to disable longer-term storage for specific tenants. for PII redaction we recommend a pre-processing step and we can also configure a no-cache mode to avoid KV cache persisting sensitive inputs. note: no-cache affects latency/cost.

[16:00] Anita: do you support SSO/SAML for the console? we need RBAC so product managers can't see infra keys.
[16:12] Priya: yes SSO via SAML/Okta, and fine-grained RBAC is available, you can map groups to roles.

[18:05] Carlos: what's the onboarding friction for the devs? how quickly can we call the API?
[18:14] Jared: we provide SDKs (python/node) and a sandbox tenant; typical devs can prototype in days. for integration with your portal we'll provide sample prompts and a client lib.

[20:30] Maya: for the pilot we need latency under 800ms p95 for short triage queries, and cost estimates — rough tpm?
[20:45] Ethan: p95 800ms is achievable in hosted with optimized model choices and batching disabled for low-latency. cost depends on token volume and model; we'll send a cost worksheet. for production if you need consistent p95s under 200ms, Dedicated with pinned capacity is the move.

[25:00] Jared: quick note — we have model catalog recommendations for triage vs summarization, we'll propose a smaller generation model for triage and a higher quality for summarization.

[28:10] Carlos: networking specifics — we need to set up VPC peering, route tables, security groups, plus a static, allowlisted IP for our SIEM ingestion. can you provide the subnet and IP ranges?
[28:30] Ethan: yes we'll share the networking checklist; for Dedicated we provide static egress IPs, for Private you control the peering and we provide accepted CIDR ranges. we'll put together a runbook.

[33:00] Samir: audit cadence — we need weekly access logs and an admin audit trail, with log retention 90 days. is that configurable?
[33:12] Priya: yes retention configurable, and we can push logs to your S3 bucket and you control lifecycle policies.

[36:00] Anita: success criteria for pilot — triage integration with <patient portal> for 500 monthly sessions, p95 <800ms, accuracy metrics (precision>85% on intent classification), and no PII leaks.
[36:20] Maya: add stakeholder signoff — product + security + infra to approve go/no-go.

[38:45] Jared: ok next steps recap, we'll: send security docs (SOC2 + encryption + KMS details), send networking checklist, create sandbox tenant + API keys, schedule a technical deep dive with ethan focusing on VPC/policies and run a small benchmark.
[39:05] Maya: yes please include a sample prompt set and recommended models so we can start early.

[41:00] Priya: timeline — we aim to have sandbox by 3/2, deep dive week of 3/8, benchmark results by 3/17, pilot start 3/22. are those dates workable?
[41:18] Carlos: tentative yes, but i'll confirm with the ops calendar.

[45:00] Ethan: about benchmarks — we'll run latency and token-cost benchmark, and also a KV cache test for note summarization. note: caching improves cost but can increase PII exposure unless configured.

[48:50] Maya: who owns the data deletion config? can we automate deletion after X days?
[48:58] Priya: yes that's a tenant-level setting, and we can automate TTL via our retention settings.

[52:00] Anita: legal/procurement — we have a standard MSA, and need DPAs for data processing, plus an attestation for FedRAMP is not required now but good to know.
[52:20] Jared: we'll loop legal and attach DPA templates, also share our standard security addendum.

[55:00] Carlos: minor note — our devs prefer curl examples over SDKs; can you include both?
[55:08] Jared: yes we'll include curl, python, node examples in the quickstart.

[58:30] Priya: recap of action items and owners (see action item list).
[59:00] Maya: thanks everyone, this was productive.
[59:05] Jared: thanks, we'll follow up with the pack and scheduling invites. bye.

End of transcript.
